metadata.title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks

nodes.name: ANN Realization Function
nodes.statement: The realization function $F^{(L)} : \mathbb{R}^{P} \to \mathcal{F}$ maps parameters $\theta$ to network functions $f_\theta$, where $P = \sum_{\ell=0}^{L-1} (n_\ell + 1) n_{\ell+1}$, with parameters initialized as iid $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Map sending neural-network parameters to the function the network computes.

nodes.name: Network Function (Preactivations and Activations)
nodes.statement: $f_\theta(x) := \tilde{\alpha}^{(L)}(x;\theta)$ with $\alpha^{(0)}(x;\theta)=x$, $\tilde{\alpha}^{(\ell+1)}(x;\theta)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_\ell}}W^{(\ell)}\alpha^{(\ell)}(x;\theta)+\beta b^{(\ell)}$, $\alpha^{(\ell)}=\sigma(\tilde{\alpha}^{(\ell)})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Recursive definition of pre-activations and activations of the network with NTK-style normalization $1/\sqrt{n_\ell}$.

nodes.name: Multi-dimensional Kernel
nodes.statement: A multi-dimensional kernel $K:\mathbb{R}^{n_0}\times\mathbb{R}^{n_0}\to\mathbb{R}^{n_L\times n_L}$ satisfying $K(x,x')=K(x',x)^T$, defining the bilinear form $\langle f,g\rangle_K=\mathbb{E}_{x,x'\sim p^{in}}[f(x)^T K(x,x') g(x')]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Symmetric matrix-valued kernel inducing a bilinear form on the function space $\mathcal{F}$.

nodes.name: Positive-definite kernel w.r.t. $\|\cdot\|_{p^{in}}$
nodes.statement: A kernel $K$ is positive-definite with respect to $\|\cdot\|_{p^{in}}$ if $\|f\|_{p^{in}}>0 \implies \|f\|_K>0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Strict positivity of the kernel-norm whenever the data-norm is positive.

nodes.name: Kernel Gradient
nodes.statement: The kernel gradient $\nabla_K C|_{f_0}\in\mathcal{F}$ is $\Phi_K(\partial^{in}_f C|_{f_0})$, satisfying $\nabla_K C|_{f_0}(x)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=1}^N K(x,x_j) d|_{f_0}(x_j)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Functional gradient of the cost computed through a kernel; generalises beyond the dataset via $K$.

nodes.name: Kernel Gradient Descent
nodes.statement: A time-dependent function $f(t)$ follows kernel gradient descent w.r.t. $K$ if $\partial_t f(t) = -\nabla_K C|_{f(t)}$; then $\partial_t C|_{f(t)} = -\|d|_{f(t)}\|_K^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Functional dynamics governed by the negative kernel gradient of the cost.

nodes.name: Tangent Kernel of Random Functions Approximation
nodes.statement: For a random linear parametrization $f_\theta^{lin}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{P}}\sum_p \theta_p f^{(p)}$, the tangent kernel is $\tilde{K}=\sum_{p=1}^P \partial_{\theta_p} F^{lin}\otimes \partial_{\theta_p} F^{lin} = \frac{1}{P}\sum_p f^{(p)}\otimes f^{(p)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Random kernel built from a finite set of random functions; converges to $K$ as $P\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK)
nodes.statement: The neural tangent kernel is $\Theta^{(L)}(\theta)=\sum_{p=1}^P \partial_{\theta_p} F^{(L)}(\theta)\otimes \partial_{\theta_p} F^{(L)}(\theta)$. The network function evolves as $\partial_t f_{\theta(t)}=-\nabla_{\Theta^{(L)}} C|_{f_{\theta(t)}}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Kernel built from the gradients of the network function w.r.t. its parameters; governs ANN gradient dynamics in function space.

nodes.name: Limiting NTK $\Theta^{(L)}_\infty$
nodes.statement: Defined recursively: $\Theta^{(1)}_\infty(x,x')=\Sigma^{(1)}(x,x')$ and $\Theta^{(L+1)}_\infty(x,x')=\Theta^{(L)}_\infty(x,x')\dot\Sigma^{(L+1)}(x,x')+\Sigma^{(L+1)}(x,x')$, with $\dot\Sigma^{(L+1)}(x,x')=\mathbb{E}_{f\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma^{(L)})}[\dot\sigma(f(x))\dot\sigma(f(x'))]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Deterministic limit of the NTK in the infinite-width regime, defined recursively in depth.

nodes.name: Activation Covariance Kernel $\Sigma^{(L)}$
nodes.statement: Defined recursively: $\Sigma^{(1)}(x,x')=\frac{1}{n_0}x^T x'+\beta^2$, $\Sigma^{(L+1)}(x,x')=\mathbb{E}_{f\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma^{(L)})}[\sigma(f(x))\sigma(f(x'))]+\beta^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Recursive covariance kernel for the Gaussian-process limit of network outputs at initialization.

nodes.name: Dual of a Lipschitz Function
nodes.statement: The dual $\hat\mu:[-1,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ of a Lipschitz $\mu:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is $\hat\mu(\rho)=\mathbb{E}_{(X,Y)}[\mu(X)\mu(Y)]$ where $(X,Y)$ is centered Gaussian with covariance $\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Definition of the dual activation as a Gaussian expectation parameterised by correlation $\rho$.

nodes.name: Least-squares Regression Cost Minimization
nodes.statement: Given a goal $f^*$ and input distribution $p^{in}$, minimize $C(f)=\frac{1}{2}\|f-f^*\|^2_{p^{in}}=\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}_{x\sim p^{in}}[\|f(x)-f^*(x)\|^2]$ over $f\in\mathcal{F}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Optimization problem: minimise the squared-error functional cost.

nodes.name: Gaussian-Process Limit of Output (Initialization)
nodes.statement: For depth $L$ with Lipschitz $\sigma$, as $n_1,\dots,n_{L-1}\to\infty$, the outputs $f_{\theta,k}$ tend in law to iid centered Gaussian processes of covariance $\Sigma^{(L)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: In the infinite-width limit at initialization, output functions converge to iid Gaussian processes with covariance $\Sigma^{(L)}$.
conclusions: Outputs $f_{\theta,k}$ are iid centered Gaussian processes

nodes.name: Convergence of NTK at Initialization
nodes.statement: For depth $L$ with Lipschitz $\sigma$, as $n_1,\dots,n_{L-1}\to\infty$, the NTK $\Theta^{(L)}$ converges in probability to a deterministic limiting kernel: $\Theta^{(L)}\to \Theta^{(L)}_\infty\otimes Id_{n_L}$.
nodes.statement_clean: At initialization, the random NTK converges in probability to a deterministic kernel in the infinite-width limit.
conclusions: Limit is deterministic and depends only on depth, $\sigma$, init variance

nodes.name: NTK Stays Constant During Training
nodes.statement: Under Lipschitz $\sigma$ with bounded second derivative, for $T$ such that $\int_0^T\|d_t\|_{p^{in}}dt$ is stochastically bounded, as $n_1,\dots,n_{L-1}\to\infty$, $\Theta^{(L)}(t)\to\Theta^{(L)}_\infty\otimes Id_{n_L}$ uniformly on $[0,T]$, and $\partial_t f_{\theta(t)}=\Phi_{\Theta^{(L)}_\infty\otimes Id_{n_L}}(\langle d_t,\cdot\rangle_{p^{in}})$.
nodes.statement_clean: The NTK remains asymptotically constant throughout training, yielding a linear functional ODE for the network function.
assumptions: $\sigma$ Lipschitz, twice differentiable, bounded second derivative
conclusions: Function-space dynamics is governed by a constant kernel

nodes.name: Positive-definiteness of Limiting NTK on the Sphere
nodes.statement: For non-polynomial Lipschitz nonlinearity $\sigma$, any input dimension $n_0$, the restriction of $\Theta^{(L)}_\infty$ to $\mathbb{S}^{n_0-1}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{n_0}:x^T x=1\}$ is positive-definite if $L\geq 2$.
nodes.statement_clean: When $\sigma$ is non-polynomial, the limiting NTK is positive-definite on the unit sphere for depth at least two.

nodes.name: A Priori Control on Weight Variation
nodes.statement: Under the setting of Theorem \ref{thm:conv-ntk-training}, for a network of depth $L+1$ and any $\ell=1,\dots,L$: $\lim_{n_L\to\infty}\cdots\lim_{n_1\to\infty}\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\|\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_\ell}}(W^{(\ell)}(t)-W^{(\ell)}(0))\|_{op}=0$ in probability.
nodes.statement_clean: Normalised weights vary negligibly during training in the sequential infinite-width limit.

nodes.name: Daniely Hermite-expansion identity for dual activations
nodes.statement: If $\mu=\sum_{i=0}^\infty a_i h_i$ is the Hermite expansion of a Lipschitz $\mu$, then its dual satisfies $\hat\mu(\rho)=\sum_{i=0}^\infty a_i^2 \rho^i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Cited Daniely lemma: the dual of a Lipschitz function has a power-series expansion with non-negative squared Hermite coefficients.

nodes.name: Schoenberg / Gneiting positive-definiteness on the sphere
nodes.statement: For $f(\rho)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty b_n\rho^n$, the kernel $K_f^{(n_0)}(x,x')=f(x^T x')$ on $\mathbb{S}^{n_0-1}\times\mathbb{S}^{n_0-1}$ is positive-definite for any $n_0\geq 1$ iff infinitely many $b_n$ are strictly positive for both even and odd $n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Cited reformulation of a Schoenberg/Gneiting result: positive-definiteness on every sphere characterised by the parity pattern of nonzero series coefficients.

nodes.name: Remark on parametrization
nodes.statement: The factors $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_\ell}}$ and $\beta$ rescale the parameter-derivatives of $F^{(L)}$ relative to LeCun initialization; in experiments $\beta=0.1$ and learning rate $1.0$ are used.
nodes.statement_clean: The paper's NTK parametrization differs from LeCun initialization by explicit scaling factors that yield the desired infinite-width asymptotics.

nodes.name: Rademacher's theorem on $\dot\sigma$
nodes.statement: By Rademacher's theorem, $\dot\sigma$ is defined everywhere except possibly on a set of zero Lebesgue measure.
nodes.statement_clean: Lipschitz $\sigma$ is differentiable almost everywhere by Rademacher's theorem.

nodes.name: Hidden-layer activations vary negligibly individually
nodes.statement: The variation of individual hidden-layer activations $\alpha^{(\ell)}_i$ during training tends to zero as the width grows, but their collective effect is significant.
nodes.statement_clean: Individual activations are nearly frozen during training in the wide limit; collective behaviour still drives learning.

nodes.name: Polynomial nonlinearity yields non-positive-definite NTK
nodes.statement: If $\sigma$ is a polynomial, the corresponding NTK $\Theta^{(2)}$ is not positive-definite on $\mathbb{S}^{n_0-1}$ for certain input dimensions $n_0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Polynomial nonlinearities break positive-definiteness of the NTK on the sphere.

nodes.name: Spectral solution for least-squares dynamics
nodes.statement: $f_t = f^* + e^{-t\Pi}(f_0-f^*) = f^* + \Delta^0_f + \sum_{i=1}^{Nn_L} e^{-t\lambda_i}\Delta^i_f$, where $f^{(i)}$ are kernel principal components and $\lambda_i$ the corresponding eigenvalues of $\Pi$.
nodes.statement_clean: Closed-form spectral expansion of the kernel-gradient flow under quadratic loss.

nodes.name: Asymptotic MAP / kernel-ridge limit
nodes.statement: $f_{\infty,k}(x) = \kappa_{x,k}^T \tilde{K}^{-1} y^* + (f_0(x) - \kappa_{x,k}^T \tilde{K}^{-1} y_0)$, with mean equal to the MAP estimate under a $\mathcal{N}(0,\Theta^{(L)}_\infty)$ prior or to kernel ridge regression as $\lambda\to 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Long-time limit of the function under kernel gradient descent matches kernel-ridgeless regression plus a vanishing Gaussian correction.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (Gaussian-process limit at initialization)
nodes.statement: By induction on $L$. Base case $L=1$: outputs are random affine functions with covariance $\Sigma^{(1)}$. Inductive step: viewing an $(L+1)$-network as an $L$-network composed with $\sigma$ and a random affine map; conditional outputs are iid Gaussian with covariance converging by the law of large numbers to $\Sigma^{(L+1)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Induction on depth using conditional Gaussianity and the law of large numbers.

nodes.name: Base case $L=1$: random affine map
nodes.statement: When $L=1$, $f_\theta(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_0}}W^{(0)}x+\beta b^{(0)}$, so all output components $f_{\theta,k}$ are independent Gaussian with covariance $\Sigma^{(1)}$.

nodes.name: Decompose $(L+1)$-network as $L$-network composed with $\sigma$ and random affine map
nodes.statement: View an $(L+1)$-network as an $L$-network mapping inputs to pre-activations $\tilde\alpha^{(L)}$, followed by elementwise $\sigma$ and a random affine map $\mathbb{R}^{n_L}\to\mathbb{R}^{n_{L+1}}$. By the inductive hypothesis, $\tilde\alpha^{(L)}_i$ are iid Gaussian with covariance $\Sigma^{(L)}$.

nodes.name: Law of large numbers on conditional covariance gives $\Sigma^{(L+1)}$
nodes.statement: Conditioned on $\alpha^{(L)}$, outputs $f_{\theta,i}$ are iid Gaussian with covariance $\tilde\Sigma^{(L+1)}=\frac{1}{n_L}\alpha^{(L)}(x;\theta)^T\alpha^{(L)}(x';\theta)+\beta^2$; by LLN as $n_L\to\infty$ this converges in probability to $\Sigma^{(L+1)}(x,x')=\mathbb{E}_{f\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma^{(L)})}[\sigma(f(x))\sigma(f(x'))]+\beta^2$, completing the induction.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem (Convergence of NTK at initialization)
nodes.statement: By induction on $L$. Base case: $\Theta_{kk'}(x,x')=\Sigma^{(1)}(x,x')\delta_{kk'}$. Inductive step: split parameters into lower-layer $\tilde\theta$ and top-layer $(W^{(L)},b^{(L)})$; by induction the lower-layer NTK converges and by the law of large numbers the top-layer contribution converges to $\Sigma^{(L+1)}\delta_{kk'}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Induction on depth with parameter splitting; uses Proposition \ref{prop:output_limit} and law of large numbers.

nodes.name: Base case $L=1$: NTK equals $\Sigma^{(1)}\delta_{kk'}$
nodes.statement: For $L=1$, summing over entries of $W^{(0)}$ and $b^{(0)}$: $\Theta_{kk'}(x,x')=\frac{1}{n_0}x^T x'\delta_{kk'}+\beta^2\delta_{kk'}=\Sigma^{(1)}(x,x')\delta_{kk'}$.

nodes.name: Split parameters $\tilde\theta$ vs. $(W^{(L)},b^{(L)})$
nodes.statement: Split the $L+1$-network into the first $L$-network with parameters $\tilde\theta$ and the top layer $(W^{(L)},b^{(L)})$. By Proposition \ref{prop:output_limit} and induction, $\tilde\alpha^{(L)}_i$ are iid Gaussian with covariance $\Sigma^{(L)}$ and $\Theta^{(L)}_{ii'}\to\Theta^{(L)}_\infty(x,x')\delta_{ii'}$.

nodes.name: LLN on lower-layer + top-layer contributions yields $\Theta^{(L+1)}_\infty$
nodes.statement: By the chain rule and induction the lower-layer contribution converges to $\Theta^{(L)}_\infty(x,x')\dot\Sigma^{(L+1)}(x,x')\delta_{kk'}$ via LLN. The top-layer contribution (sum over $W^{(L)},b^{(L)}$) converges to $\Sigma^{(L+1)}\delta_{kk'}$. Adding gives $\Theta^{(L+1)}_\infty\delta_{kk'}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem (NTK constant during training)
nodes.statement: Induction on $L$. Use back-propagated training directions $d^{(\ell)}$, apply Lemma \ref{lem:control-w} to bound $\|W^{(L)}(t)/\sqrt{n_L}\|_{op}$, then a Grönwall-type argument on $A(t)$ shows weights and pre-activations vary at rate $1/\sqrt{n_L}$, implying NTK varies at the same rate.
nodes.statement_clean: Induction with Grönwall control on a combined activation/weight quantity $A(t)$.

nodes.name: Base case $L=1$ and induction setup
nodes.statement: Base case $L=1$: NTK does not depend on parameters, so it is constant during training. Inductive step: split the $L+1$-network into a lower $L$-network with parameters $\tilde\theta$ and top layer $(W^{(L)},b^{(L)})$; smaller network follows training direction $d'_t=\dot\sigma(\tilde\alpha^{(L)})(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_L}}W^{(L)})^T d_t$.

nodes.name: Bound $\|d'_t\|$ via Lemma \ref{lem:control-w}
nodes.statement: Since $\sigma$ is $c$-Lipschitz, $\|d'_t\|_{p^{in}}\leq c\|\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_L}}W^{(L)}(t)\|_{op}\|d_t\|_{p^{in}}$. Applying Lemma \ref{lem:control-w} reduces bounding $\|\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_L}}W^{(L)}(t)\|_{op}$ to bounding it at $t=0$, which is bounded by LLN. Apply induction hypothesis to smaller network.

nodes.name: Grönwall control on combined quantity $A(t)$
nodes.statement: Define $A(t)=\|\alpha^{(L)}_i(0)\|_{p^{in}}+c\|\tilde\alpha^{(L)}_i(t)-\tilde\alpha^{(L)}_i(0)\|_{p^{in}}+\|W^{(L)}_i(0)\|_2+\|W^{(L)}_i(t)-W^{(L)}_i(0)\|_2$. Cauchy-Schwarz and ODE bounds give $\partial_t A(t)\leq\frac{\max\{c^2\|\Theta^{(L)}_\infty\|_{op},1\}}{\sqrt{n_L}}\|d_t\|_{p^{in}}A(t)$. Grönwall: $A(t)\leq A(0)\exp(\cdot)\to A(0)$ in probability as $n_L\to\infty$.

nodes.name: NTK summands vary at rate $1/\sqrt{n_L}$ from top layer
nodes.statement: Top-layer derivatives $\partial_{W^{(L)}_{ij}}f_{\theta,j'}(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_L}}\alpha^{(L)}_i(x;\theta)\delta_{jj'}$ together with $1/\sqrt{n_L}$ activation drift give NTK summands varying at rate $n_L^{-3/2}$, hence NTK varies at $1/\sqrt{n_L}$.

nodes.name: Lower-layer NTK contribution: $W^{(L)}_{ij}$ and $\dot\sigma$ vary at rate $1/\sqrt{n_L}$
nodes.statement: For lower-layer parameters: by induction $\Theta^{(L)}\to\Theta^{(L)}_\infty\delta_{ii'}$. The connection weights $W^{(L)}_{ij}$ vary at rate $1/\sqrt{n_L}$. Bounded second derivative of $\sigma$ implies $\partial_t \dot\sigma(\tilde\alpha^{(L)}_i)=O(\partial_t \tilde\alpha^{(L)}_i)$, also $1/\sqrt{n_L}$. Combining yields constant-NTK conclusion.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (A priori control on weights)
nodes.statement: Express weight and activation variations through back-propagated directions $d^{(\ell)}$ and sub-network NTKs; derive recursive polynomial bounds; assemble $A(t)=\sum_k a^{(k)}(0)+c\tilde a^{(k)}(t)+w^{(k)}(0)+\tilde w^{(k)}(t)$ and apply nonlinear Grönwall to obtain $A(t)\to A(0)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Polynomial recursive bounds plus nonlinear Grönwall yield the vanishing of $\tilde w^{(\ell)}(t)$ in the sequential limit.

nodes.name: Express dynamics via back-propagated directions and sub-network NTKs
nodes.statement: Write $\partial_t \tilde\alpha^{(\ell)}=\Phi_{\Theta^{(\ell)}}(\langle d^{(\ell)}_t,\cdot\rangle_{p^{in}})$ and $\partial_t W^{(\ell)}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_\ell}}\langle\alpha^{(\ell)},d^{(\ell+1)}_t\rangle_{p^{in}}$, with layer-wise back-propagated directions $d^{(\ell)}_t=\dot\sigma(\tilde\alpha^{(\ell)})(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_\ell}}W^{(\ell)})^T d^{(\ell+1)}_t$ (and $d^{(L+1)}_t=d_t$).

nodes.name: Recursive polynomial bounds on $\|d^{(\ell)}_t\|$ and $\|\Theta^{(\ell)}\|_{op}$
nodes.statement: Set $w^{(k)}(t)=\|\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_k}}W^{(k)}(t)\|_{op}$, $a^{(k)}(t)=\|\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_k}}\alpha^{(k)}(t)\|_{p^{in}}$. Recursive bounds give $\|d^{(\ell)}_t\|\leq c^{L+1-\ell}\prod_{k=\ell}^L w^{(k)}(t)\|d_t\|$ and $\|\Theta^{(\ell+1)}\|_{op}\leq\mathcal{P}(a^{(1)},\dots,a^{(\ell)},w^{(1)},\dots,w^{(\ell)})$ for a polynomial $\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.name: Construct $A(t)$ and bound its derivative
nodes.statement: Define $\tilde a^{(k)},\tilde w^{(k)}$ as variations from $t=0$ and $A(t)=\sum_{k=1}^L a^{(k)}(0)+c\tilde a^{(k)}(t)+w^{(k)}(0)+\tilde w^{(k)}(t)$. Combine the polynomial bounds to obtain $\partial_t A(t)\leq \frac{1}{\sqrt{\min n_k}}\tilde{\mathcal{Q}}(A(t))\|d_t\|_{p^{in}}$ for a polynomial $\tilde{\mathcal{Q}}$ with positive coefficients.

nodes.name: Apply nonlinear Grönwall to conclude $A(t)\to A(0)$
nodes.statement: $A(0)$ is stochastically bounded under the sequential limit: $w^{(\ell)}\to 0$ and $a^{(\ell)}$ converges by Proposition \ref{prop:output_limit}. Nonlinear Grönwall (e.g. \cite{dragomir}) gives $A(t)$ uniformly bounded on $[0,\tau]$ with $\tau\to T$ as $\min n_k\to\infty$; the $1/\sqrt{\min n_k}$ prefactor forces $\partial_t A\to 0$ uniformly, hence $A(t)\to A(0)$ and $\tilde w^{(\ell)}\to 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (Positive-definiteness on the sphere)
nodes.statement: Decompose $\Theta^{(L+1)}=\dot\Sigma^{(L)}\Theta^{(L)}+\Sigma^{(L+1)}$ so positive-definiteness reduces to that of $\Sigma^{(L+1)}$. Show inductively from $\Sigma^{(2)}$. Express $\Sigma^{(2)}(x,x')=\nu(x^T x')$; the Hermite expansion has infinitely many even and odd nonzero coefficients (Lemma \ref{lem:daniely}), so Theorem \ref{thm:schoenberg} yields positive-definiteness.
nodes.statement_clean: Reduce to base level $\Sigma^{(2)}$, use Daniely's Hermite identity and the Schoenberg/Gneiting characterisation.

nodes.name: Recursive decomposition $\Theta^{(L+1)}=\dot\Sigma^{(L)}\Theta^{(L)}+\Sigma^{(L+1)}$
nodes.statement: For $L\geq 1$, $\Theta^{(L+1)}=\dot\Sigma^{(L)}\Theta^{(L)}+\Sigma^{(L+1)}$. The first summand is positive semi-definite (product of two PSD kernels), so positive-definiteness of $\Theta^{(L+1)}$ reduces to that of $\Sigma^{(L+1)}$.

nodes.name: Inductive lift: positive-definiteness of $\Sigma^{(2)}$ implies $\Sigma^{(L)}$ for $L\geq 2$
nodes.statement: Using $\Sigma^{(L+1)}(x,x')=\mathbb{E}_f[\sigma(f(x))\sigma(f(x'))]+\beta^2$, $\sum_{i,j}c_i c_j\Sigma^{(L+1)}(x_i,x_j)=\mathbb{E}[(\sum_i c_i\sigma(f(x_i)))^2]+(\beta\sum c_i)^2$ vanishes only when all $c_i=0$ if $\Sigma^{(L)}$ is positive-definite (so $f(x_i)$ are non-degenerate Gaussian) and $\sigma$ non-constant. Hence by induction $\Sigma^{(L)}$ is PD for $L\geq 2$.

nodes.name: Reduce $\Sigma^{(2)}$ to $\hat\mu$ via change of variables
nodes.statement: $\Sigma^{(2)}(x,x')=\mathbb{E}_{(X,Y)\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\tilde\Sigma)}[\sigma(X)\sigma(Y)]+\beta^2$ with $\tilde\Sigma$ depending on $\frac{1}{n_0}x^T x'$. A change of variables yields $\mathbb{E}[\sigma(X)\sigma(Y)]+\beta^2=\hat\mu(\frac{n_0\beta^2+x^T x'}{n_0\beta^2+1})+\beta^2$ where $\mu(x)=\sigma(x\sqrt{1/n_0+\beta^2})$ and $\hat\mu$ is its dual.

nodes.name: Hermite expansion: infinitely many nonzero $a_i$ since $\sigma$ non-polynomial
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:daniely}, $\hat\mu(\rho)=\sum_i a_i^2 \rho^i$ where $\mu=\sum_i a_i h_i$. Since $\sigma$ is non-polynomial, $\mu$ is non-polynomial, hence infinitely many $a_i$ are nonzero.

nodes.name: Apply Schoenberg/Gneiting: $\Sigma^{(2)}=\nu(x^T x')$ with both even and odd nonzero coefficients
nodes.statement:
Write $\Sigma^{(2)}(x,x')=
u(x^T x')$ with $
u(ho)= eta^2+\sum_i a_i((n_0 eta^2+ho)/(n_0 eta^2+1))^i$. Power series of $
u$ has infinitely many nonzero even and odd terms; Theorem ef{thm:schoenberg} yields positive-definiteness of $\Sigma^{(2)}$ on $\mathbb{S}^{n_0-1}$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Convergence of NTK on the unit circle (depth 4)
nodes.statement: Empirical illustration: $\Theta^{(4)}(x_0,x)$ for $x_0=(1,0)$ and $x=(\cos\gamma,\sin\gamma)$ on the unit circle, widths $n=500,10000$, ten initializations, fitting $f^*(x)=x_1 x_2$ with least-squares; wider networks have smoother, less variable NTK and the kernel barely changes after 200 steps.
nodes.statement_clean: Numerical demonstration that the NTK concentrates and stays nearly constant for wide networks.

nodes.name: Kernel regression on the unit circle
nodes.statement: Train ANNs of widths $n=50,1000$ on a least-squares cost on 4 unit-circle points for 1000 steps with learning rate $1.0$; compare to the theoretical $t\to\infty$ Gaussian distribution computed from $\Theta^{(4)}_\infty$ and $\Sigma^{(4)}$ (approximated via $n=10000$).
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical match between finite-width network function distributions and the theoretical Gaussian limit at convergence.

nodes.name: Convergence along principal components on MNIST
nodes.statement: Compute first three NTK kernel principal components on a batch of $N=512$ MNIST digits using $n=10000$, with eigenvalues $\lambda_1=0.0457, \lambda_2=0.00108, \lambda_3=0.00078$. Set $f^* = f_{\theta(0)}+0.5 f^{(2)}$ and verify exponential decay $\|g_t\|_{p^{in}}=0.5 e^{-\lambda_2 t}$ along the principal direction for widths $n=100,1000,10000$.
nodes.statement_clean: MNIST experiment confirming exponential decay along NTK kernel principal components, matching the theory.
